verses.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin.

Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me. Don’t throw me from your presence, and don’t take your Holy Spirit from me. Restore to me the joy of your salvation. Uphold me with a willing spirit.

He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us for our iniquities. For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his loving kindness towards those who fear him. As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.
I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn’t hide my iniquity. I said, I will confess my transgressions to the LORD, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin.
Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man to whom the LORD doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit.
If you, LORD, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand? But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared.
Come now, and let’s reason together,” says the LORD: “Though your sins are as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.
I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity, and passes over the disobedience of the remnant of his heritage? He doesn’t retain his anger forever, because he delights in loving kindness. He will again have compassion on us. He will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
Sins overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our transgressions.
I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.
Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to the LORD, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
It is because of the LORD’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his mercies don’t fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But one to whom little is forgiven, loves little.” He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.
He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.” Jesus said to him, “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”

Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?” She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.”
For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.

When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit! If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”

He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.”
There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
But God commends his own love towards us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
The law came in that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly.
Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
In him we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace.
But God, being rich in mercy, for his great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—.
Who delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love, in whom we have our redemption, the forgiveness of our sins.
Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness. I will remember their sins and lawless deeds no more.
Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.
Not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit.
Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out, so that there may come times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord.

When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do. But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Come to me, all you who labour and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
For you, Lord, are good, and ready to forgive, abundant in loving kindness to all those who call on you.
The LORD is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great loving kindness. The LORD is good to all. His tender mercies are over all his works.
They looked to him, and were radiant. Their faces shall never be covered with shame.
Don’t remember the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions. Remember me according to your loving kindness, for your goodness’ sake, LORD.
If my people who are called by my name will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
But you have mercy on all men, because you have power to do all things, and you overlook the sins of men to the end that they may repent.
How great is the mercy of the Lord, and his forgiveness to those who turn to him!
I will heal their waywardness. I will love them freely; for my anger is turned away from them.
The LORD, your God, is amongst you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.

messages.text: There is no sin greater than God's mercy. None.
The Sacrament of Confession is waiting for you. The priest is there to welcome you, not to condemn you.
Guilt that leads you back to God is a grace. Shame that pushes you away is not from Him.
Jesus came for sinners, not for the perfect. That includes you.
The father of the prodigal son ran to meet him. God runs to meet you too.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has God removed your sins from you.
Peter denied Jesus three times. Jesus asked him three times, Do you love Me? Love restored him.
Once you are forgiven, you are forgiven. Do not keep picking up what God has thrown into the sea.
Say it honestly: Lord, I am sorry. He hears, and He forgives.
Saint Augustine lived far from God for years and became one of the Church's greatest saints.
Jesus said to the woman caught in sin, Neither do I condemn you. Go, and sin no more.
God is not waiting to punish you. He is waiting to embrace you.
Pray the Act of Contrition slowly and mean each word.
Your past does not disqualify you from God's love.
Make amends where you can. Then trust God with what you cannot fix.
The good thief asked Jesus to remember him, and Jesus promised him Paradise that same day.
Heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine who need no repentance.
Jesus told Saint Faustina that the greater the sinner, the greater the right to His mercy.
Do not let the devil tell you that you have gone too far. Christ's blood is enough.
God gives you a new heart and a new spirit. Ask Him for it.
You are more than your worst mistake.
Forgive yourself, because God has forgiven you. To refuse His forgiveness is to make yourself a stricter judge than God.
Mary Magdalene loved much because she was forgiven much.
Your sins, though they are like scarlet, shall be as white as snow.
Every saint has a past, and every sinner has a future.
Jesus, I trust in You. These words from the Divine Mercy image are for you today.
If you have not been to Confession in a long time, do not be afraid. Just tell the priest, and he will help you.
There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
God's mercy is new every morning. Today is a fresh start.
Guilt can become gratitude when you receive God's forgiveness.
Ask Saint Mary Magdalene, Saint Augustine and Saint Peter to pray for you. They know the way home.
God does not remember the sins He has forgiven. Let your heart rest in that.
Honesty before God brings freedom. Hiding brings heaviness.
Let your sorrow turn into love. Love covers a multitude of sins.
Pray Psalm 51, King David's prayer after his great sin. God restored him, and He can restore you.
If you have hurt someone, ask God for the courage to say sorry. Reconciliation brings peace.
God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance, not to despair.
Jesus told the disciples, Whose sins you forgive are forgiven. Confession is His gift to you.
You are not your sin. You are a child of God who is being healed.
Begin again. Saints are simply sinners who kept getting up.
Lord, have mercy. It is the simplest prayer, and God always answers it.
The Cross shows how far God will go to forgive you.
After Confession, thank God and walk in freedom. You are made new.
God is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
Let go of the weight. Christ already carried it to the Cross.
Mercy is God's favourite gift to give. Ask for it boldly.
Saint Paul called himself the foremost of sinners, and God made him an apostle.
Humility is not hating yourself. It is letting God love you as you are and make you new.
Tomorrow, try again with God's help. He is patient with you.
Rest tonight. If you have asked for mercy, you have received it.
